documents.title: 行政の進化と革新のための生成AIの調達・利活用に係るガイドライン
documents.issuing_body: デジタル社会推進会議幹事会 (Digital Society Promotion Council Executive Committee)
documents.implementation_notes: This guideline (DS-920) is classified as 'Normative' within the Digital Society Promotion Standard Guidelines framework, making it binding on national government ministries and agencies for government information systems incorporating generative AI (specifically LLM-based text generation AI). Full application begins FY2026 (April 2026), with FY2025 systems expected to comply as much as possible. The guideline establishes a CAIO role at each ministry, an Advisory Board for advanced AI use, and detailed procurement/contract checklists. It explicitly excludes systems handling classified information, national security, or public safety. Local governments and independent administrative agencies are only expected (not required) to follow it.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document frames AI governance primarily around the safe and appropriate use of generative AI in government operations, emphasizing risk management (hallucination, information leakage, harmful outputs, bias) alongside benefit realization. The core logic is that safety guardrails and risk management must accompany active promotion of AI use—'利活用促進とリスク管理を表裏一体で進める'. This is fundamentally a public/consumer safety framing applied to government systems and the citizens they serve. Secondary frames include innovation enablement (accelerating administrative innovation, encouraging active adoption) and economic competitiveness (Japan's international AI competitiveness, startup support in public procurement).

documents.title: 農業分野におけるAI・データに関する契約ガイドライン～農業分野のノウハウの保護とデータ利活用促進のために～
documents.issuing_body: 農林水産省 (Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries of Japan)
documents.implementation_notes: This is a contractual guideline (契約ガイドライン) for AI and data use in the agricultural sector, focused on know-how protection and data utilization. It provides model contracts and term sheets for data/know-how provision, AI R&D commissioning, and third-party data sharing. It is non-binding guidance referencing METI AI contract guidelines. No penalties or mandatory compliance dates are specified.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is a contract guideline from Japan's Ministry of Agriculture aimed at promoting data utilization and protecting agricultural know-how in AI development. The primary framing is enabling innovation—facilitating AI adoption in agriculture through clear contract frameworks, IP protection, and data sharing arrangements. Economic competitiveness appears as a secondary frame through references to AI Strategy 2019 goals and commercialization. Consumer/public safety appears modestly through liability and personal data handling provisions.

documents.title: ＡＩ戦略推進関係省庁会議（第2回）議事要旨
documents.issuing_body: Cabinet Office / Secretariat of Japan
documents.implementation_notes: Meeting minutes of the 2nd AI Strategy Promotion Inter-Ministerial Conference. Key items: AI bill legislative progress reported; Digital Agency presented draft AI government procurement/utilization guidelines and requested ministries appoint Chief AI Officers (CAIO); FSA published AI Discussion Paper on financial sector use cases; METI introduced GENIAC-PRIZE program for generative AI social implementation. Chair noted Diet deliberations touched on human-centric AI, local government AI use, and deepfake pornography risks. Goal stated as making Japan 'the world's most AI-friendly country for development and utilization'.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is primarily framed around enabling rapid AI adoption and social implementation ('world's most AI-friendly country for development and utilization', promoting generative AI deployment programs, and accelerating nationwide AI implementation), with national economic competitiveness as a closely paired secondary rationale.

documents.title: 生成AIの導入・活用に向けた実践ハンドブック 実証結果報告書
documents.issuing_body: こども家庭庁 (Children and Families Agency, Japan)
documents.implementation_notes: This is a pilot project report (実証結果報告書) accompanying a practical handbook on generative AI adoption in child and family policy domains. Conducted by ABeam Consulting on behalf of the Children and Families Agency. 14 local government entities participated with 45 use cases across document creation, data analysis, chatbot deployment, image recognition, and audio transcription. No binding obligations or penalties are established; findings are intended to inform voluntary adoption guidance.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is primarily framed around enabling practical adoption of generative AI in government (child and family services), with the stated purpose of advancing 'appropriate use' and sharing best practices via a handbook. Risk governance is subsidiary—security and data handling are addressed as operational concerns within the pilot, not as the central rationale. The driving logic is to demonstrate how AI can improve public service efficiency and quality, making innovation_enablement the dominant frame, with consumer/public safety secondary due to attention to data privacy and child-related sensitive information.

documents.title: the AI Act (Overview) (Provisional Translation)
documents.issuing_body: Cabinet Office / Secretariat of Japan
documents.implementation_notes: This is a provisional translation of an overview document. The act is primarily a promotion and framework law rather than a strict regulatory regime. Partial enforcement began 4 June 2025, full enforcement 1 September 2025. Binding obligations on business operators appear limited to cooperation duties. Detailed requirements will likely emerge via guidelines and the AI Basic Plan.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document primarily frames AI governance around economic competitiveness and innovation promotion, emphasizing that Japan is lagging behind in AI development and needs to enhance international competitiveness while aiming to be the friendliest country for AI development. National security and human rights are mentioned but are secondary to the economic and innovation rationale.

documents.title: AIの利用・開発に関する契約チェックリスト
documents.issuing_body: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
documents.implementation_notes: This document is a practical contract checklist published by METI in February 2025, aimed at businesses engaging in AI utilization and development. It is non-binding guidance to assist businesses—especially those unfamiliar with AI legal practice—in reviewing contract terms related to inputs, outputs, personal data handling under Japan's Act on the Protection of Personal Information (APPI), security, and log retention. It references the 'AI事業者ガイドライン' (AI Business Operator Guidelines v1.01, November 2024) and the prior 2019 'AI・データの利用に関する契約ガイドライン'. No penalties or enforcement authorities are named; the document is purely advisory.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is primarily framed around protecting business users (consumers/enterprises) from legal and data-handling risks when contracting for AI services. It explicitly cites concerns about legal risks not being properly examined and data being used for unexpected purposes or provided to third parties causing unforeseen harm. While innovation enablement and economic competitiveness are mentioned as context, the checklist's core purpose is risk management and protection of data subjects and contracting parties—a consumer/public safety framing. Fundamental rights (personal data protection under Japan's APPI) appears as a strong secondary frame.

documents.title: ＡＩと著作権に関する考え方について
documents.issuing_body: Agency for Cultural Affairs (Japan)
documents.implementation_notes: Document explicitly states it has no legal binding force ('本考え方自体が法的な拘束力を有するものではない'). It is interpretive guidance on how existing Japanese copyright law applies to generative AI, covering training/learning stage and generation/use stage. The document notes it may be revised as case law, technology, and international developments evolve. It references Article 30-4 (non-enjoyment-purpose use) and Article 47-5 of the Copyright Act as relevant rights-limitation provisions. No prohibited practices are formally established; the document clarifies existing law rather than imposing new rules.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is primarily framed around protecting the intellectual property rights of creators and rights holders while balancing those rights against the need for fair use in AI development. The central concern is rights protection under copyright law, with secondary attention to enabling AI innovation and maintaining Japan's competitiveness in the AI field.

documents.title: AI・データの利用に関する契約ガイドライン 1.1版（全体版）
documents.issuing_body: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
documents.implementation_notes: This is a non-binding guideline (version 1.1, revised December 2019 from June 2018 original) providing model contract clauses and considerations for data contracts covering three types: data provision contracts, data creation contracts, and data sharing platform contracts. It explicitly states it does not restrict freedom of contract. Revision addressed alignment with guidelines on limited-provision data (限定提供データ).
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is primarily framed around enabling data-driven innovation through clear contractual guidelines. Its stated purpose is to facilitate data transactions and AI utilization, with references to 'data-driven innovation creation' and IoT/AI platform case studies. Secondary framings include fundamental rights (personal data protection, GDPR compliance) and national security (export controls under FEFTA for dual-use technologies).

documents.title: 人工知能戦略専門調査会の設置について
documents.issuing_body: 人工知能戦略本部 (AI Strategy Headquarters)
documents.implementation_notes: This document establishes the AI Strategy Expert Panel (人工知能戦略専門調査会) under Cabinet Order No. 281 of Reiwa 7 (2025), pursuant to the Act on Promotion of Research, Development and Utilization of AI-Related Technologies (Act No. 53 of Reiwa 7). The panel is tasked with investigating guidelines (Article 13), research and surveys (Article 16), and basic plans (Article 18). Members are appointed by the Prime Minister from persons with expertise in AI. The panel may invite external experts and establish working groups.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document establishes an expert panel to promote research, development, and utilization of AI-related technologies. Its primary stated purpose is advancing AI R&D and application, framing governance as an enabler of innovation rather than a risk-mitigation body.

documents.title: Governance Guidelines for Implementation of AI Principles
documents.issuing_body: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
documents.implementation_notes: Document is explicitly non-binding (Ver. 1.0). It is framed as a voluntary guideline supporting METI's Social Principles of Human-centric AI. Action targets are described as general objectives for all AI companies, while implementation examples are discretionary. The document is intended as a living document subject to agile governance revision.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document frames AI governance primarily as a mechanism to facilitate AI deployment and support voluntary company efforts, with governance serving to enable rather than restrict AI. The stated aim is 'supporting the implementation of AI principles required for the facilitation of deployment of AI.' Secondary framing includes managing negative impacts on society and users.

documents.title: AI Governance in Japan Ver. 1.1
documents.issuing_body: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
documents.implementation_notes: This is a strategy/analysis report from an expert group, not binding regulation. It maps out a layered AI governance architecture including non-binding guidelines, international standards, and sector-specific regulations, but stops short of mandating any specific requirements. The document identifies future issues including monitoring/enforcement design. Confidence is moderate as the document text provided is primarily the introduction and table of contents.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document primarily frames AI governance as a challenge of enabling innovation while managing risks at acceptable levels. The explicit goal is to avoid hindering innovation while addressing concerns, and governance is framed as a tool for operationalizing AI principles in ways conducive to Japanese industrial competitiveness and social acceptance. Consumer safety and social stability are secondary concerns embedded in the risk management language.

documents.title: Guidelines for Ensuring the Proper Development and Use of AI-Related Technologies (Provisional Translation)
documents.issuing_body: Artificial Intelligence Strategic Headquarters
documents.implementation_notes: This guideline is based on Article 13 of Japan's AI Act (Act No. 53 of 2025) but is explicitly designed to encourage voluntary compliance rather than impose binding mandates. Stakeholders are expected to respond 'at a suitable level, taking into account their scale, position, and the risks posed by AI.' The document is a provisional English translation and defers to the Japanese original for accuracy. No explicit civil or criminal penalties are specified; enforcement is primarily through voluntary self-governance and PDCA cycles.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document's primary framing centers on ensuring AI is safe and appropriate for all users and stakeholders, emphasizing harm prevention (hallucinations, deepfakes, disinformation, cyberattacks, bias/discrimination) and accountability across the AI lifecycle. It consistently uses safety, transparency, and human-centric principles as the core governance rationale, directed at protecting citizens, consumers, and society from AI harms. Innovation enablement and fundamental rights are strong secondary frames, reflecting Japan's dual goal of promoting beneficial AI while protecting rights and dignity.

documents.title: 人工知能関連技術の研究開発及び活用の適正性確保に関する指針
documents.issuing_body: Cabinet Office / Secretariat of Japan
documents.implementation_notes: This guideline is issued under Article 13 of the AI Promotion Act (Act No. 53 of 2025). It promotes voluntary and proactive compliance rather than mandating specific binding obligations. Actors are expected to apply measures proportionate to their scale, role, and AI risk level. The guideline references the Hiroshima AI Process International Code of Conduct and ISO/IEC 42001 as applicable international norms. The document is intended to be reviewed and updated in an agile manner as AI technology evolves.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document frames AI governance primarily around protecting human dignity, basic human rights, fairness, and non-discrimination, while also balancing innovation promotion. Key elements listed—human-centricity, fairness, privacy, accountability, transparency—are rights-based. Innovation enablement is a strong secondary frame, with the document repeatedly emphasizing that safety and rights protections should not impede AI's social implementation and innovation.

documents.title: AI Guidelines for Business Ver 1.0 (Provisional Translation)
documents.issuing_body: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
documents.implementation_notes: The Guidelines are voluntary and intended as a reference for business operators. They follow an agile governance/living document approach and are to be updated as needed. Generative AI is explicitly included in scope. Non-business users and data providers are excluded from the target audience.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document consistently grounds AI governance in respect for human dignity, autonomy, human rights, diversity, and inclusion. The three basic philosophies—Dignity, Diversity & Inclusion, and Sustainability—explicitly center on human rights and individual well-being. Common Guiding Principles require that AI not violate constitutionally or internationally guaranteed human rights. Secondary frames include social stability (avoiding divisions within society, ensuring fair outcomes) and innovation enablement (promoting open innovation, sustainable economic growth).

documents.title: 「農業分野におけるAI・データに関する契約ガイドライン」に関するQ＆A(PDF : 493KB)
documents.issuing_body: 農林水産省 (Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Japan)
documents.implementation_notes: 本文書は「農業分野におけるAI・データに関する契約ガイドライン」のQ&A改訂版。農林水産省補助事業等を活用する場合のみ要件化対象。自己資金導入の場合は要件化対象外だが準拠が望ましいとされる。チェックリストおよび契約ひな形が農林水産省HPに公開されている。
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is a Q&A guide for AI/data contracts in agriculture, primarily framed around enabling safe data sharing to promote smart agriculture adoption. The core stated reason for governance is to facilitate data utilization while protecting farmers' know-how, allowing them to 'safely provide data.' This is innovation enablement (promoting smart agriculture) with a secondary consumer/public safety frame around preventing data leaks and protecting agricultural trade secrets.

documents.title: 第14回 ＡＩ戦略会議 議事要旨
documents.issuing_body: Cabinet Office / Secretariat of Japan
documents.implementation_notes: 本文書は2025年6月2日開催の第14回AI戦略会議の議事要旨。同年5月28日に成立した「人工知能関連技術の研究開発及び活用の推進に関する法律」（AI法）の概要およびAI戦略本部設置・AI基本計画策定・指針整備の方向性が議論された。統合イノベーション戦略2025のAIパート案も審議。デジタル庁は生成AI調達・利活用ガイドラインを5月27日に策定済み。AIと著作権・IPをめぐる権利ルール整備、学習用データ基盤の整備が課題として提起された。
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document consistently frames AI governance around Japan becoming the world's most AI-friendly nation, maintaining international competitiveness especially in content/IP industries against China, Korea, and the US, and balancing innovation promotion with risk management. Economic competitiveness language dominates, with specific references to export industries, startup creation, and competitive threats from foreign AI tools.

documents.title: 人工知能基本計画
documents.issuing_body: 内閣（閣議決定）/ Cabinet of Japan
documents.implementation_notes: This is Japan's first AI Basic Plan (人工知能基本計画), adopted by Cabinet decision on 23 December 2025 under Article 18(1) of the AI Act (令和7年法律第53号). It is a government strategy document, not binding legislation. Key pillars: (1) accelerating AI utilization, (2) strengthening AI development capacity, (3) leading AI governance, (4) continuous societal transformation. AISI to be doubled in staffing immediately. No explicit prohibited practices stated; focus is on innovation promotion balanced with risk response. No formal compliance deadlines specified.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document's central framing is Japan's competitive position in AI development globally. The subtitle '日本再起' (Japan's revival/resurgence) and repeated language about falling behind major nations, the need for 'counter-offensive' (反転攻勢), reducing digital deficit, and becoming 'the world's most AI-friendly country' all foreground economic competitiveness. Innovation enablement is a strong secondary frame. National security and consumer/public safety risks are acknowledged but positioned as conditions to be managed in service of the primary competitiveness goal.

documents.title: 生成AIの導入・活用に向けた実践ハンドブック
documents.issuing_body: こども家庭庁 (Children and Families Agency, Japan)
documents.implementation_notes: Document explicitly states it has no binding or compulsory force ('法的その他いかなる意味においても拘束力・強制力を持つものではない'). It is a practical handbook for generative AI adoption in the child and family services domain, based on pilot project findings as of March 31, 2025. Recommends human oversight of all AI outputs, compliance with personal information protection laws, and staff literacy training. Encourages referencing related ministry guidelines before adoption.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is primarily framed around enabling the practical adoption of generative AI in childcare and child-rearing public services to improve efficiency and service quality. The stated purpose is to help municipalities and childcare facilities appropriately introduce and utilize generative AI, reducing administrative burdens so staff can spend more time with children and families. Risk governance (personal data, hallucinations, bias, IP rights) is treated as a condition for responsible enablement, not the central rationale. Consumer/public safety concerns about AI outputs affecting children are a significant secondary frame, as are rights-related concerns around personal information and bias.

documents.title: コンテンツ制作のための生成AI利活用ガイドブック
documents.issuing_body: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
documents.implementation_notes: This is a non-binding guidebook (ガイドブック) intended to provide practical guidance for content production industries (game, anime, advertising) on appropriate use of generative AI. It explicitly states it does not interpret copyright law or guarantee legality. It is positioned below binding government guidelines (AI事業者ガイドライン) and is intended as a practical companion to those instruments. Content reflects information as of June 2024.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document's primary stated reason for governance is protecting intellectual property rights and other legal interests (著作権等の権利・利益の保護) of creators and rights holders when using generative AI in content production. Rights protection language appears in the stated purpose, throughout use-case descriptions, and in the positioning section. A secondary frame of innovation enablement is also strong, as the document encourages appropriate and active use of generative AI to enhance creativity and efficiency. Consumer/public safety appears in references to preventing misinformation and controlling inappropriate outputs.

documents.title: 生成AIサービスの利用に関する注意喚起等について
documents.issuing_body: Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC)
documents.implementation_notes: This is a guidance/alert document (注意喚起) from Japan's PPC issued on 2023-06-02, addressing use of generative AI services with personal data. It references the Act on the Protection of Personal Information (個人情報保護法) as the binding legal basis, but the document itself is advisory guidance rather than binding regulation. The PPC separately issued a notice to OpenAI. Guidance covers both private sector entities and public sector bodies.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is primarily framed around protecting individual rights and interests (権利利益) through proper handling of personal information under Japan's Personal Information Protection Law. The core justification is safeguarding privacy and personal data rights when using generative AI services. Secondary framing acknowledges innovation benefits and public safety concerns about inaccurate outputs.

documents.title: 人工知能技術戦略実行計画
documents.issuing_body: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
documents.implementation_notes: This is a government implementation plan (実行計画) translating the 2017 AI Technology Strategy and industrialization roadmap into concrete targets with deadlines and responsible ministries. It is not legally binding. No prohibited practices or enforcement penalties are specified. The document covers R&D, human resource development, data/tool environment, venture support, and public understanding across priority domains: productivity, health/medical/care, mobility, and information security.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document frames AI governance primarily as a competitiveness challenge, explicitly noting Japan's lag behind the US and China in research, talent, data, and venture support, and calling for Japan to 'win fierce competition' and 'lead the world.' The industrialization roadmap, sectoral productivity targets, and market acquisition goals further reinforce this frame. Innovation enablement is secondary, as the plan details R&D and social implementation programs. Labor/talent transition appears through extensive workforce development sections.

documents.title: ＡＩ戦略 2022
documents.issuing_body: 統合イノベーション戦略推進会議 (Integrated Innovation Strategy Promotion Council)
documents.implementation_notes: AI戦略2022 is a non-binding national strategy document building on AI Strategy 2019 and 2021. It sets strategic goals (目標0–4) covering crisis resilience (AI for National Resilience, Planetary Resilience), social implementation of AI, and responsible/trustworthy AI. No specific compliance deadlines, penalties, or enforcement mechanisms are defined. The document references the 'Human-Centered AI Social Principles' (2019) as the foundational ethical framework.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document frames AI governance primarily through economic competitiveness: it explicitly aims to strengthen Japan's industrial competitiveness, achieve top-runner status in real-world industries, improve labor productivity to match the US and Germany, and build international AI networks to expand market reach. National resilience (disaster response, pandemic preparedness) and social stability are strong secondary frames, especially in Strategic Goal 0. Innovation enablement appears throughout as a means to achieve these goals.

documents.title: 医療デジタルデータのAI研究開発等への利活用に係るガイドライン
documents.issuing_body: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
documents.implementation_notes: Guideline focuses on pseudonymized medical information (仮名加工情報) under Japan's Act on Protection of Personal Information for use in AI R&D and medical device product development. Excludes: clinical trial data, anonymous processing (匿名加工情報), cross-border data transfers, advanced privacy-enhancing technologies, generative AI legal risks, and the Next-Generation Medical Infrastructure Act (次世代医療基盤法). Practical procedures for creating pseudonymized data from diagnostic text, physiological function tests, medical images, genetic test data, and multimodal data are provided.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document opens by explicitly framing medical AI data utilization in the context of intensifying global R&D competition, positioning Japan's data governance as a matter of competitive capacity. The preface warns that privacy law 'greatly affects data resources that are the source of competitiveness.' Simultaneously, it foregrounds patient rights protection and privacy as a core constraint, making fundamental_rights a strong secondary frame. Innovation enablement is also present as the guideline aims to remove legal barriers to product development.

documents.title: 「医療デジタルデータの AI 研究開発等への利活用に係るガイドライン」について
documents.issuing_body: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
documents.implementation_notes: This is a notice (事務連絡) transmitting a guideline developed under a research grant. The guideline covers use of medical digital data for AI R&D, focusing on legal basis clarification and pseudonymization procedures. It is non-binding guidance circulated to healthcare institutions, research bodies, local governments, and industry associations. Confidence is moderate as the actual guideline content is in an attachment not included in the normalized text.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document focuses on clarifying legal bases for using medical digital data in AI research, with emphasis on proper handling of personal medical information (pseudonymized data procedures), reflecting a fundamental rights framing around privacy and lawful data use. Secondary concerns include patient safety and enabling innovation.

documents.title: 「医療デジタルデータの AI 研究開発等への利活用に係るガイドライン」の留意点について
documents.issuing_body: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
documents.implementation_notes: This document is a clarification notice (事務連絡) issued alongside a pre-existing guideline on AI use of medical digital data published 2024-09-30. The guideline is explicitly non-binding, positioned as a reference tool for pseudonymized data handling under the Personal Information Protection Act. It covers only medical information stored at healthcare institutions for use in medical device R&D, excluding Next-Generation Medical Infrastructure Act data and registry data. No independent enforcement mechanisms are created by this document.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document is primarily framed around protecting individual rights—specifically the privacy and data protection rights of patients whose sensitive medical information is used in AI research. It emphasizes that medical information is 'extremely sensitive' personal data subject to strict legal protections, and that the guideline aims to ensure 'social trust' in the use of medical information. Secondary framings include consumer/public safety (ensuring proper handling of medical data in device development) and innovation enablement (facilitating AI-based medical device R&D).

documents.title: 初等中等教育段階における生成AIの利活用に関するガイドライン
documents.issuing_body: 文部科学省初等中等教育局
documents.implementation_notes: This is Ver. 2.0 of the guideline, revising the provisional Ver. 1.0 published July 2023. The document explicitly states it does not uniformly prohibit or mandate use of generative AI in schools ('学校現場での生成AIの利活用を一律に禁止したり義務付けたりするものではない'). It serves as reference material for school staff and education boards. No penalties or enforcement mechanisms are specified. Future revisions are anticipated as technology evolves.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document primarily frames AI governance in schools as enabling appropriate and effective use of generative AI to support student learning and teacher capabilities, while managing associated risks. The central thrust is how to utilize AI tools beneficially within the existing educational framework, emphasizing AI literacy, human-centered principles, and practical guidance for appropriate adoption rather than restriction. Consumer/public safety and fundamental rights appear as secondary framings through attention to information security, privacy, copyright, and age-appropriate use.

documents.title: Social Principles of Human-Centric AI
documents.issuing_body: Cabinet Office / Secretariat of Japan
documents.implementation_notes: This is a high-level strategy/principles document with no binding legal force. The document explicitly states it operates in a 'non-regulatory, non-binding framework.' It covers broad societal principles rather than specific technical mandates. Safety requirements extracted are aspirational statements addressed to society, government, and industry rather than enforceable obligations. The document was established by an advisory council under the Cabinet Office and is intended to inform future AI strategy and policy.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document centers on human dignity, diversity, and protection of fundamental rights as the primary justification for AI governance. It repeatedly invokes constitutional rights, non-discrimination, privacy protection, and human-centric values. While innovation and competitiveness appear, they are subordinate to the rights-based and human dignity framework.

documents.title: 大学・高専における生成AIの教学面の取扱いについて（周知）
documents.issuing_body: 文部科学省 高等教育局 専門教育課・大学教育・入試課 (Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology)
documents.implementation_notes: This is a non-binding circular (事務連絡) from MEXT providing guidance to universities and colleges on handling generative AI in teaching. It does not impose legal obligations but strongly encourages institutions to develop their own guidelines. The document is advisory in nature, using language like '望ましい' (desirable) and 'お願いします' (request). No penalties or formal enforcement mechanisms are specified.
documents.framing_rationale_summary: The document primarily frames generative AI governance in higher education around enabling appropriate use and building AI literacy, while managing risks such as academic integrity, misinformation, and data privacy. The dominant tone is guidance on how to utilize AI effectively rather than restrict it, with safety concerns treated as secondary considerations.
